segments.t: Welcome back to Domashniy Arest! Deeply wounded by the slanderous smear campaign accusing his grandfather of being a Nazi collaborator, Ivan Samsonov has disappeared on a drinking binge. In his troubled sleep, he experiences a feverish wartime dream where he crawls across a foggy battlefield, accompanied by the famous Soviet song 'The Final Battle'. Let's listen to the scene in Russian first.
Где мы? Кругом дым и воронки.
Мы ползём по грязи так долго!
А я домой в Россию хочу.
Я так давно не видел маму.
Now let's examine Ivan's dramatic wartime dream sequence line by line. The lines weave together iconic lyrics from the famous song with Ivan's inner torment over his grandfather's reputation.
Где мы? Кругом дым и воронки.
'Where are we? Smoke and bomb craters are all around.' Ivan looks around in confusion at the foggy war landscape.
'Crawl forward! We have almost arrived.' The fellow soldier urges him to keep moving through the mud.
Мы ползём по грязи так долго!
'We have been crawling through mud for so long!' Ivan struggles forward on his elbows across the battlefield.
'Tomorrow the final battle awaits us.' The phrase echoes the iconic Soviet wartime song of the same name.
'Just a little more, just a little bit!' This famous lyric conveys exhaustion and desperate hope.
'This battle will be the hardest one.' The superlative adjective highlights the ultimate sacrifice required.
'My grandfather was not a traitor!' Even in his feverish nightmare, Ivan defends his family honor.
'Everyone knows the truth. Hold on, soldier!' The comrade soldier offers reassurance and encouragement.
А я домой в Россию хочу.
'And I want to go home to Russia.' The object-form directional noun expresses deep homesickness.
'Soon we will return home.' This phrase indicates an eventual successful homecoming.
Я так давно не видел маму.
'I haven't seen my mother in so long.' The object-form noun refers affectionately to his mother.
'Mother is waiting for you alive.' The short adjective agrees in gender and case with the pronoun.
'I will not betray my native land!' Ivan affirms his steadfast loyalty to his motherland.
'Then wake up, Ivan! It is time for you.' The dream begins to dissolve as reality calls him back. Now let's listen to Ivan's dream sequence once more in Russian.
Где мы? Кругом дым и воронки.
Мы ползём по грязи так долго!
А я домой в Россию хочу.
Я так давно не видел маму.
Ivan's dream reflects the heavy burden of wartime memory and patriotism in modern Russian life. See you next time!
